inconsistencies: Chain: #36592 (macOS SDK 15) must be reviewed and merged before #36593 (Qt 6.12), which explicitly requires it; they were originally two bands apart.
Chain: #36554 (reject warnings in feature detection, -msse4.1 for SHA-NI) is a stated prerequisite for #31507 (clang-cl on Windows); review #36554 first.

Chain: #36042 (GCC 13) and #36036 (Clang 19) are both prerequisites for #36033 (C++23 RFC) and are the same kind of change; they were originally banded differently. Review the two bumps before deciding on #36033.

Overlapping scope: #36082 (Guix release builds in CI) subsumes much of #35774 (test cross-built macOS arm64 binaries). Decide the division of labour; #36082 is the broader mechanism, #35774 the narrower and already-rebased one.
Overlapping scope: #36147 replaces the cross-compiled BSD CI jobs with native VM jobs, which would make the BSD SDK download caching in #35722 moot. Review #36147 first.

Warning-flag cluster: #36167 (-Wunused), #35911 (-Wmissing-noreturn), #36268 (-Wextra-semi), #36623 (-Wunreachable-code-aggressive) and #36704 (-Wdocumentation-unknown-command) all add compiler flags plus wide mechanical fixups and will conflict with each other; several are also blocked on the same Minisketch/libmultiprocess subtree updates. Sequencing them matters more than any individual merge.

IPC build cluster: #32387 (Windows IPC), #36060 (KJ exception check), #36556 (capnp TSan patches), #35454 (external libmultiprocess targets), #36679 (i686 IPC CI) and #19460 (wallet -ipcconnect) all touch the same multiprocess build stack and subtree; coordinate subtree bumps to avoid repeated churn.

Release-binary path hygiene appears twice: #36270 (depends paths in release binaries) and #36708 (DISTSRC debug-prefix-map); they solve adjacent halves of the same problem and should be reviewed together.
result.notes: The category is dominated by CI and toolchain maintenance; only two PRs reach P1, both about release integrity (silent wrong-source depends builds and signature-verification accepting revoked keys). The P2 band is reserved for release-binary security/portability, supported-platform build breakage, release-build CI coverage, and the compiler-minimum transition chain. Several original scores appear to have been assigned independently and left prerequisites (#36592, #36554, #36036) ranked well below the work they unblock; those were corrected.
